artists.biography: Rick Springfield (born Richard Lewis Springthorpe; 23 August 1949) is an Australian singer-songwriter, musician, and actor. He was a member of pop rock group Zoot from 1969 to 1971 and then started his solo career with his début single "Speak to the Sky" reaching the top 10 in Australia. In mid-1972, he relocated to the United States. He had a No. 1 hit with "Jessie's Girl" in 1981 in both Australia and the US. He received the Grammy Award for Best Male Rock Vocal Performance for "Jessie's Girl". He followed with four more top 10 US hits, "I've Done Everything for You", "Don't Talk to Strangers", "Affair of the Heart" and "Love Somebody". His two US top 10 albums are Working Class Dog (1981) and Success Hasn't Spoiled Me Yet (1982). As an actor, he portrayed Dr. Noah Drake on the daytime drama General Hospital, from 1981 to 1983 and during 2005 to 2008 and 2012, returning in 2013 for the shows 50th anniversary with son/actor Liam Springthorpe. In 2010, Springfield published his autobiography, Late, Late at Night: A Memoir.

perplexity.description:
Working Class Dog is the fifth studio album by Australian rock musician Rick Springfield, released in 1981 by RCA Victor. The album blends melodic rock and pop, featuring catchy hooks, polished production, and Springfield's signature vocal style. It marked a turning point in his career, combining his rock roots with accessible pop sensibilities, and showcased his talents as a multi-instrumentalist, with contributions from notable musicians such as Robben Ford and Neil Giraldo on guitar.

This album stands as Springfield's commercial breakthrough, ending a five-year gap between studio releases and revitalizing his music career. It produced his biggest hit, "Jessie's Girl," which topped the charts and earned him the 1982 Grammy Award for Best Rock Vocal Performance, Male. The album was certified Platinum in the United States and sold over three million copies, establishing Springfield as a major figure in early 1980s rock and pop. Its success also led to a distinctive legacy, with the album cover—featuring Springfield's Bull Terrier, Ronnie—becoming iconic in its own right.
